tasks.title: Decide how additional organisations connect Instagram
tasks.detail: A Meta app per organisation means separate verification, App Review, secret and callback each time; one operator app serving many businesses changes the developer of record and what Meta reviews (verify Tech Provider rules). Align the gateway's per-workspace credential storage with the choice.
tasks.done_when: A merged ADR names the model, the per-org onboarding steps and any Meta review required.

tasks.title: Draft the multi-organisation contract pack
tasks.detail: Terms of service or MSA, an Art. 28 DPA template, a public sub-processor page with change notice, an acceptable-use policy including the minors rules, a security and tenant-isolation statement, export and deletion at termination, liability terms and a BAA policy for US customers, reviewed by a lawyer.
tasks.done_when: The lawyer-reviewed pack is ready and the sub-processor page is published.

tasks.title: Build the operator console with audited, time-limited support access
tasks.detail: A cross-workspace view of health, usage, cost, feature flags, channel status and provisioning with no client data; support access is an org-approved, expiring, fully audited break-glass grant.
tasks.done_when: The operator sees per-workspace health and cost without client data, and a support session needs approval, expires and appears in that org's audit log.

tasks.title: Meter per-workspace usage and set up billing
tasks.detail: Attribute Claude tokens, SMS and WhatsApp messages, storage and seats to each workspace, agree the pricing model, and invoice monthly through a billing provider per the contract pack.
tasks.done_when: A month of usage for two workspaces reconciles with provider invoices within 2% and a test invoice is issued.

tasks.title: Package the onboarding template for the next organisation
tasks.detail: A provisioning script (workspace, roles, ladders, empty playbook, master-data import) plus an org checklist reusing P0 (Meta connection and verification, App Review, TikTok check, exports, price list, consent forms, roster, app enrolment), the Q1-Q9 questionnaire, a compliance checklist (scope memo, DPIA addendum, privacy notice, claims and banned lists, clinician owner, residency) and a timeline.
tasks.done_when: A dummy organisation is provisioned in under an hour, a cross-tenant test is refused, and the checklist and questionnaire are published.

tasks.title: Sign organisation 2 and complete its contracts and compliance onboarding
tasks.detail: Signed MSA and DPA, Q1-Q9 answers, scope memo and DPIA addendum, Meta connection and verification, TikTok eligibility, export requests, a price list and a named clinician sign-off owner.
tasks.done_when: Org 2's contracts and checklist are filed and its platform applications are submitted.

tasks.title: Provision organisation 2, run its history pipeline and start shadow mode
tasks.detail: Provision in org 2's chosen residency, load staff, rota and master data, run the history pipeline for its own playbook, connect channels once approved and start shadow, logging template gaps.
tasks.done_when: Org 2 runs in shadow with cross-tenant tests green and the onboarding template updated.

tasks.title: Hand over admin control and reduce the builder's access to the agreed least privilege
tasks.detail: Org admins log into every account in the register, confirm 2FA and recovery, and rotate at least one production key themselves using the runbook; the builder is then downgraded or removed as the organisation decides.
tasks.done_when: Every register row shows admins verified by a live login and the builder at the agreed level, with the owner's dated sign-off.

tasks.title: Operate the platform on weekly, monthly and quarterly cadences
tasks.detail: Weekly: merge dependency updates and triage alerts and DLQs. Monthly: service review (uptime vs SLA, incidents, coordinator SLAs, nightly QA findings, cost vs budget), a restore drill and a compatibility_date bump via staging. Quarterly: remove leavers (always within 24 h of departure), review users, grants, MCP tokens, API keys and admins on every vendor account, rotate secrets per the inventory, check renewals and re-run the security checklist. Yearly: an app admin completes Meta's Data Use Checkup before its deadline (missing it deactivates the app and every permission must go back through App Review), and Business Verification, app roles and the privacy and deletion URLs are confirmed current.
tasks.done_when: The ops log has a dated entry for every cadence, each quarter has an owner-signed access attestation, no secret exceeds its rotation period, and Meta's Data Use Checkup is completed each year before its deadline.

tasks.title: Run the playbook and compliance governance cadence
tasks.detail: Weekly: the playbook owner decides every queued proposal within 7 days with reasons, with clinician sign-off on clinical items, and rejected ideas are recorded. Monthly: review claims, banned phrases and the price list and retire expired items. Yearly or after a major change: review the DPIA, ROPA, retention schedule and training.
tasks.done_when: The change log shows a decision on every proposal within 7 days and clinician sign-off on every clinical change, plus dated monthly and annual reviews.

tasks.title: Hold a weekly AI channel review
tasks.detail: Review handoff reasons, guardrail blocks, refusals, co-pilot edits, nightly QA findings and cost, and re-tune thresholds through PRs that must pass the eval gate.
tasks.done_when: A review note with actions is logged every week.

tasks.title: Run the quarterly policy, regulation and platform API watch
tasks.detail: Check Meta Platform Terms and messaging policy, Graph API version deprecations, TikTok terms, eligibility and API versions, WhatsApp policy, the Anthropic Usage Policy and terms, Cloudflare terms, sub-processors and the laws in the scope memo, and open a task for each change.
tasks.done_when: Each quarter has a dated entry with findings and follow-up tasks, and no deprecated API version is in use.

tasks.title: Track Claude model and API changes and gate every change on the evals
tasks.detail: Watch deprecations and release notes for every model and beta in use (reply engine, call brief, extraction, jobs). Before changing model, effort or beta header, run the eval and red-team suites, compare cost and latency, and get the owner's sign-off.
tasks.done_when: A dated model register lists each route's model, beta headers and retirement dates, and every change links to an eval report.

this_week.why_now: Sign a standard mutual NDA on day 1 so the builder can be invited to the vault and vendor accounts this week.
Q1 (country), Q2 (procedure type) and Q8 (admin access) block most of P0; start the 5-working-day clock for answers or recorded defaults.
The repo is public under a personal account today and must be private before any organisation-specific file is committed.
The operating model decides who owns Cloudflare, Anthropic and GitHub. It no longer waits for the 5-day answer window: decide it at the kickoff so P0-10 and P0-11 can start this week.
The privacy lead, clinician and legal reviewer sign the scope memo, privacy notice, claims list and playbook, so every legal task waits on them.
Every vendor login uses the vault and admin alias, and the Instagram audit can't start without them.
This is the first link in the Meta chain (portfolio, Business Verification, App Review), and scrapers or private-API tools risk a ban today.
Business Verification is submitted from the portfolio, so it has to exist in the legal name first.

Business Verification is the longest-lead item on the path to Instagram and Meta controls its pace; submit in week 1. If "Start verification" is greyed out, first create the bare Business-type Meta app owned by the portfolio; Meta usually enables verification only once an app or WhatsApp account is connected.
The TikTok registration country decides between the direct API, a partner or manual mode, and an eligible account should apply in weeks 1-2.
The Anthropic org must exist so the DPA (and a BAA request if US clients) is in place before any client data reaches Claude.
Cloudflare hosts everything; the Paid plan and correct ownership are needed before IaC, the export bucket and the gateway.
The Meta app settings, App Review and the TikTok application all need a live privacy URL.
Exporters must be named and the staff roster collected before exports are requested and before masking and lint can be built.
The signed price list feeds the claims list, Playbook v0, get_price and the lint, all on the shadow-mode path.
The builder can start the monorepo skeleton now without any client data or open answers.
No dependencies: staff can export saved replies, FAQ documents and call scripts now. Playbook v0 and the eval set are built from them.

decisions_needed.question: Q1: In which country are the organisation and its TikTok account registered, and where are clients located?
decisions_needed.why: Decides GDPR/UK GDPR vs HIPAA, data residency and the Claude route, TikTok API eligibility (EEA/UK/CH blocked), advertising and under-18 rules, SMS sender rules and breach deadlines.

decisions_needed.question: Q2: What procedures does the organisation offer (medical, cosmetic, dental, hair, other)?
decisions_needed.why: Sets whether data is health data, which prescription-only medicine and claims rules apply, minimum ages, clinician sign-off scope, consent forms and the treatment-plan model.

decisions_needed.question: Q3: Which records show which past DM leads converted (bookings, clinic software, payments, call logs)?
decisions_needed.why: Outcome labels drive the history analysis and Playbook v1; thin records trigger staff labelling or proxy labels.

decisions_needed.question: Q4: How many DMs arrive per day, and how many staff are there in which roles?
decisions_needed.why: Sizes budgets, spend caps and load tests, the rota and SLA ladder, role templates, training, and device and MCP seat counts.

decisions_needed.question: Q5: Which tools are in use today (calendar, clinic software, payments, WhatsApp Business, spreadsheets)?
decisions_needed.why: Decides integrate vs replace, migration sources, existing WhatsApp numbers and automations to switch off, and processor contracts.

decisions_needed.question: Q6: What is the payment model (deposits, packages, instalments) and which provider?
decisions_needed.why: Shapes payment wording in the playbook, the price list, money policies, the ledger and instalments, and consumer-credit and cancellation checks.

decisions_needed.question: Q7: Which languages do DMs arrive in?
decisions_needed.why: Every approved string (disclosure, escalation, minors, banned phrases, templates), the masking audit, eval coverage and language routing must exist per language.

decisions_needed.question: Q8: Which business accounts exist, and who has admin access to the Meta Business portfolio and TikTok Business Center?
decisions_needed.why: Without admin access nothing on the Instagram path can start: account audit, portfolio, Business Verification, Meta app, App Review and exports.

decisions_needed.question: Q9: Is the organisation OK starting in shadow and then co-pilot mode for 2-4 weeks before autopilot?
decisions_needed.why: Sets the gate criteria and timeline; working back from App Review approval (~week 7), autopilot realistically lands in weeks 11-13 instead of week 10.

decisions_needed.question: Operating model: will an operator own the multi-tenant platform (Cloudflare, Anthropic, GitHub), or will each organisation get its own deployment?
decisions_needed.why: This must be decided before any platform account is created. Otherwise organisation 2's data could end up in organisation 1's accounts, and code ownership and reuse stay unclear.

decisions_needed.question: Where may health data live: is HIPAA in scope, which D1/R2 jurisdiction applies, and is first-party Claude inference acceptable or must it run in an EU region via Vertex AI or Bedrock?
decisions_needed.why: R2 jurisdiction is fixed when a bucket is created and HIPAA needs a Cloudflare Enterprise BAA, so this decision has to come before any personal data is stored. Anthropic HIPAA readiness is organisation-wide and permanent and blocks the Batch API; first-party Claude inference runs in the US or globally only; the Vertex AI or Bedrock EU route has no Anthropic Batch endpoint or server-side fallbacks (verify).

decisions_needed.question: Should comment-to-DM (instagram_business_manage_comments) and the HUMAN_AGENT tag be requested in the first App Review?
decisions_needed.why: Adding them later needs a second review, and leaving them out removes comment handling from P3.

decisions_needed.question: Which TikTok route (direct API, partner, or manual), and what date triggers the fallback?
decisions_needed.why: Partners cannot get around the EEA/UK/CH block. The chosen route decides what is built and paid for.

decisions_needed.question: What is the Instagram contingency trigger date, and which fallback applies if Business Verification or App Review slips?
decisions_needed.why: If this is agreed in week 1, a slip costs days instead of weeks.

decisions_needed.question: Should WhatsApp use a new dedicated number or migrate the existing WhatsApp Business app number?
decisions_needed.why: Migration and coexistence rules affect current use, and staff alerts in P2 depend on it.

decisions_needed.question: Which coordinator calling setup will be used, and which public number does the AI give out?
decisions_needed.why: Clients must recognise the callback and never see personal numbers. The AI's handoff wording depends on this.

decisions_needed.question: What exactly goes into the co-pilot MVP scope, and what moves to P4/P5?
decisions_needed.why: Without a freeze, P2 holds over 70 builder tasks and the week-9 co-pilot date slips.

decisions_needed.question: What numeric thresholds apply to the shadow-to-co-pilot and co-pilot-to-autopilot gates?
decisions_needed.why: Fixing them before shadow starts stops the targets moving once data arrives.

decisions_needed.question: Which model and effort per route, and what monthly AI budget (Opus 5.5 by default; Sonnet 5.5 only if the owner trades quality for cost)?
decisions_needed.why: This sets cost per reply, spend caps and the history batch budget.

decisions_needed.question: Will staff use company or personal phones, and will apps be distributed via MDM or redemption codes?
decisions_needed.why: This sets the device policy, clinical photo capture, remote-wipe ability and native app distribution.

decisions_needed.question: Should calls be recorded (off by default)?
decisions_needed.why: Recording needs notices, consent checks and retention rules, and it changes the SOP.

decisions_needed.question: What are the deposit, cancellation, no-show, refund and instalment policies?
decisions_needed.why: These policies drive payment wording, distance-contract and consumer-credit checks, and the ledger.

decisions_needed.question: Should existing clinic tools and the calendar be integrated or replaced?
decisions_needed.why: This decides the migration scope and whether calendar sync or a double-entry rule is built.

decisions_needed.question: Should an external pen test be commissioned before go-live?
decisions_needed.why: Budget and timing must be known before the security review is signed.

decisions_needed.question: May testimonials and before/after photos be used in DMs or marketing?
decisions_needed.why: Until the policy is approved the AI shares none. This affects the playbook and later retention work.

decisions_needed.question: Cloudflare plan: does the owner accept Workers Paid ($5/month plus metered R2, D1 and Queues usage) instead of the free tier the request asked for?
decisions_needed.why: The free plan's per-request CPU limit, 24-hour queue retention and lack of Containers block password hashing, the reply tool loop and multi-GB history processing.
